dek: Haleakalā's two waterfalls, Waimoku and Makahiku Falls, are in the Kīpahulu district past Hāna. See the Pīpīwai Trail distance, fees and the sunrise rule.
overview: Haleakalā National Park's Kīpahulu district is 12 miles past Hāna on the Hāna Highway, and offers waterfalls, ocean views and a cultural landscape.

We cover two waterfalls, both filed under Hāna. Waimoku Falls is the bigger hike at 1.8 miles one way on the Pīpīwai Trail, and it has the most visitor reviews of the two. Makahiku Falls is also inside the park but has no published distance. The Pools of ʻOheʻo are closed to entry, and the park says to view them from the Kūloa Point Trail.
fallsIntro: Waimoku Falls is the one with a hike length. Makahiku Falls is the other named waterfall in the same district.
plan: The published walk is the Pīpīwai Trail to Waimoku Falls, 1.8 miles one way. Makahiku Falls has its own page, but we can't say whether you pass it on the way to Waimoku, so we haven't added the two together. To reach the trailhead, continue 12 miles past Hāna on the Hāna Highway. The $30 vehicle fee lasts three days and covers both the summit and Kīpahulu districts.
flow: The gauge at Oheo Gulch near Kīpahulu (USGS 16501200) is only about 0.2 mile from Makahiku Falls. From 2019 through 2024 its average daily flow peaked in March at about 101 cubic feet per second and was lowest in August at about 17.
East Maui streams can rise and fall quickly, and this gauge is on a different gulch from Waimoku Falls, so use it as a rough guide.
feesLead: The vehicle fee lasts three days, not seven, and covers both the summit and Kīpahulu.
access: A vehicle reservation is required to enter the summit between 3 a.m. and 7 a.m. for sunrise. It costs $1 on Recreation.gov, is not waived on fee-free days, and doesn't apply to the Kīpahulu waterfalls, so you don't need it for an afternoon on the Pīpīwai Trail. The waterfall trail is on the other side of the island from the summit road, so plan the two separately.
safety: The park closes the Pools of ʻOheʻo to entry because of safety concerns, so enjoy the view from the Kūloa Point Trail. It also says Kīpahulu is often wet. We have no other warning on file for the Pīpīwai Trail, so check conditions at the visitor center.
